projects.summary: Create a small local repository that connects each analysis change to a test and a result interpretation.

milestones.title: Organize the project
milestones.deliverable: Source, tests, sample input, and generated-output conventions.
milestones.acceptance: Raw observations and generated artifacts have clearly different roles.

milestones.title: Record a baseline
milestones.deliverable: A reviewed commit with a runnable known fixture.
milestones.acceptance: The staged diff contains only intended shareable content.

milestones.title: Change one assumption
milestones.deliverable: A second commit with an explained analysis or validation change.
milestones.acceptance: The commit includes a relevant test and a meaningful message.

milestones.title: Write a comparison
milestones.deliverable: A note connecting changed code to changed results.
milestones.acceptance: The note names input identity, code version, and remaining uncertainty.

testPlan: Fresh checkout or clean folder can run the sample.
Generated results do not silently replace source evidence.
extensions: Add a small changelog of scientific assumptions.
Practice a branch locally before learning remote collaboration.
portfolio: Two coherent commits with reviewed diffs.
constraints: Publishing to a remote is optional and deliberate.
Do not commit credentials or private logs.
Git history is not your only backup.

projects.title: Dependency-aware experiment workflow
projects.summary: Coordinate several harmless analysis stages and prove that failures, partial outputs, and background work are handled correctly.

milestones.title: Draw dependencies
milestones.deliverable: A graph of fixture generation, analysis, comparison, and report steps.
milestones.acceptance: Every consumer depends on a verified completed producer.

milestones.title: Implement sequentially
milestones.deliverable: A readable runner using fixed commands and explicit status checks.
milestones.acceptance: A failure stops only the dependent work and is identified accurately.

milestones.title: Add one independent task
milestones.deliverable: An optional background metadata task with captured PID and wait status.
milestones.acceptance: The report waits for required tasks and does not confuse launch with completion.

milestones.title: Inject failures
milestones.deliverable: A test matrix of missing inputs, failing stubs, and stale output files.
milestones.acceptance: No failing case yields a false success report.

testPlan: A deliberately failing producer prevents its consumer.
A stale file cannot satisfy current-run completion.
Owned background tasks are waited on and statuses checked.
extensions: Add a documented timeout using a supported tool only when needed.
Compare sequential and limited parallel execution after correctness is established.
constraints: Use harmless stubs or offline analysis, not physical propulsion equipment.
Manage only processes started by the workflow.
Do not parallelize stages that share mutable outputs.

glossary.definition: A program that interprets commands and provides a scripting language.
glossary.example: Bash interprets a quoted path and invokes a program.

glossary.definition: The interface through which a user interacts with a shell.
glossary.example: One terminal application can host Bash or PowerShell.

glossary.definition: One value passed to a command after shell interpretation.
Syntax controlling expansion and word boundaries.
The default stream a program reads.
glossary.example: A pipeline supplies grep with text on stdin.

glossary.definition: The default stream for ordinary program results.
glossary.example: A count printed for another program to consume.

glossary.definition: A separate stream conventionally used for diagnostics.
A numeric outcome returned by a completed command.
A connection from one command’s stdout to another’s stdin.
glossary.example: grep selects lines before wc counts them.

glossary.definition: A shell or tool pattern matching filenames.
glossary.example: *.log selects a class of names under specified rules.

glossary.definition: A separate shell execution environment with its own variable state.
glossary.example: A loop in a pipeline may not update a parent counter.

glossary.definition: A structured sequence of separate values in Bash.
glossary.example: An array holds paths without joining them into one string.

glossary.definition: The current editable files in a Git repository.
glossary.example: A script change appears here before it is staged.

glossary.definition: The selected snapshot prepared for the next Git commit.
The property that repeating an operation has the same intended effect as doing it once.
glossary.example: A validated directory-creation step can tolerate reruns, while blind log appending may duplicate records.
